```{r baseline-validation, include=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# GRAPH 1: BASELINE VALIDATION
# ============================================================

library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(patchwork)

# ============================================================
# LOAD DATA
# ============================================================

df <- read_csv(
  "Graph_1_Baseline_Validation.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Check data
View(df)

# ============================================================
# PUBLICATION THEME
# ============================================================

theme_pub <- theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(
      size = 12,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    
    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 10,
      colour = "black"
    ),
    
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 12,
      face = "bold",
      hjust = 0
    ),
    
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    
    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 10
    ),
    
    legend.position = "top",
    
    panel.border = element_rect(
      colour = "black",
      fill = NA,
      linewidth = 0.6
    ),
    
    plot.margin = margin(6, 6, 6, 6)
  )


# ============================================================
# PANEL A: UPDATE RATE
# ============================================================

p1 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = threshold)) +
  
  # Theoretical curve
  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = theoretical_update_rate,
      linetype = "Theory"
    ),
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  
  # Simulation values
  geom_point(
    aes(
      y = update_rate,
      shape = "Simulation"
    ),
    size = 2.7
  ) +
  
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(
      "Theory" = "dashed"
    )
  ) +
  
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(
      "Simulation" = 16
    )
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "(a) Update rate",
    x = "Threshold",
    y = "Update rate"
  ) +
  
  theme_pub


# ============================================================
# PANEL B: MEAN AoI
# ============================================================

p2 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = threshold)) +
  
  # Theoretical curve
  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = theoretical_mean_aoi,
      linetype = "Theory"
    ),
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  
  # Simulation values
  geom_point(
    aes(
      y = mean_aoi,
      shape = "Simulation"
    ),
    size = 2.7
  ) +
  
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(
      "Theory" = "dashed"
    )
  ) +
  
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(
      "Simulation" = 16
    )
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "(b) Mean AoI",
    x = "Threshold",
    y = "Mean AoI"
  ) +
  
  theme_pub


# ============================================================
# PANEL C: MSE
# ============================================================

p3 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = threshold)) +
  
  # Theoretical curve
  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = theoretical_mse,
      linetype = "Theory"
    ),
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  
  # Simulation values
  geom_point(
    aes(
      y = mse,
      shape = "Simulation"
    ),
    size = 2.7
  ) +
  
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(
      "Theory" = "dashed"
    )
  ) +
  
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(
      "Simulation" = 16
    )
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "(c) MSE",
    x = "Threshold",
    y = "MSE"
  ) +
  
  theme_pub


# ============================================================
# COMBINE ALL THREE PANELS
# ============================================================

graph1 <- (p1 | p2 | p3) +
  plot_layout(
    guides = "collect"
  ) &
  theme(
    legend.position = "top"
  )


# Display graph
graph1


# ============================================================
# SAVE HIGH-QUALITY PNG
# ============================================================

ggsave(
  filename =
    "Graph_1_Baseline_Validation.png",
  
  plot = graph1,
  
  width = 10,
  height = 3.6,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)


# ============================================================
# SAVE VECTOR PDF
# ============================================================

ggsave(
  filename =
    "Graph_1_Baseline_Validation.pdf",
  
  plot = graph1,
  
  width = 10,
  height = 3.6,
  units = "in"
)
```


```{r accuracy-vs-packet-loss, include=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# GRAPH 2: ACCURACY VERSUS PACKET LOSS
# ============================================================

library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)

# ============================================================
# LOAD DATA
# ============================================================

df <- read_csv(
  "Graph_2_Accuracy_vs_Packet_Loss.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

View(df)

# ============================================================
# PREPARE DATA FOR PLOTTING
# No MSE or CI values are recalculated
# ============================================================

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    loss_percent = loss_probability * 100,

    signal_label = recode(
      signal,
      "Temp" = "Temperature",
      "Moist" = "Soil moisture"
    ),

    feedback_label = recode(
      feedback_model,
      "ack" = "ACK",
      "no_ack" = "No ACK"
    ),

    estimator = factor(
      estimator,
      levels = c(
        "hold",
        "weighted_drift",
        "local_linear",
        "full_drift"
      ),
      labels = c(
        "Hold",
        "Weighted drift",
        "Local linear",
        "Full drift"
      )
    )
  )


# ============================================================
# CREATE GRAPH
# ============================================================

graph2 <- ggplot(
  df,
  aes(
    x = loss_percent,
    y = mse_mean,
    colour = estimator,
    shape = estimator,
    group = estimator
  )
) +

  # Connecting lines
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.85
  ) +

  # Saved confidence intervals
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = mse_ci_low,
      ymax = mse_ci_high
    ),
    width = 1.0,
    linewidth = 0.45,
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +

  # Simulation points
  geom_point(
    size = 2.5,
    stroke = 0.7
  ) +

  # Four requested panels:
  # Temperature ACK / No ACK
  # Soil moisture ACK / No ACK
  facet_grid(
    signal_label ~ feedback_label,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +

  # Publication-friendly colour-blind-safe palette
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Hold" = "#0072B2",
      "Weighted drift" = "#D55E00",
      "Local linear" = "#009E73",
      "Full drift" = "#CC79A7"
    )
  ) +

  # Shapes make the graph interpretable even in grayscale
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(
      "Hold" = 16,
      "Weighted drift" = 17,
      "Local linear" = 15,
      "Full drift" = 18
    )
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 50, 10),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0.02, 0.04)
    )
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Packet loss probability (%)",
    y = "Mean squared error (MSE)",
    colour = "Estimator",
    shape = "Estimator"
  ) +

  theme_classic(
    base_size = 12
  ) +

  theme(

    # Axis titles
    axis.title = element_text(
      size = 12,
      face = "bold"
    ),

    # Axis numbers
    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 10,
      colour = "black"
    ),

    # Panel header background
    strip.background = element_rect(
      fill = "grey95",
      colour = "black",
      linewidth = 0.6
    ),

    # Panel header text
    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 11,
      face = "bold",
      colour = "black"
    ),

    # Legend
    legend.position = "top",

    legend.title = element_text(
      size = 11,
      face = "bold"
    ),

    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 10
    ),

    # Panel border
    panel.border = element_rect(
      colour = "black",
      fill = NA,
      linewidth = 0.6
    ),

    # Clean margins
    plot.margin = margin(
      8, 8, 8, 8
    )
  )


# ============================================================
# DISPLAY GRAPH
# ============================================================

graph2


# ============================================================
# SAVE HIGH-RESOLUTION PNG
# ============================================================

ggsave(
  filename =
    "Graph_2_Accuracy_vs_Packet_Loss.png",

  plot = graph2,

  width = 8.5,
  height = 6.5,
  units = "in",

  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)


# ============================================================
# SAVE VECTOR PDF
# ============================================================

ggsave(
  filename =
    "Graph_2_Accuracy_vs_Packet_Loss.pdf",

  plot = graph2,

  width = 8.5,
  height = 6.5,
  units = "in"
)
```


```{r weighted-drift-improvement, include=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# GRAPH 3: WEIGHTED-DRIFT IMPROVEMENT
# FINAL PUBLICATION VERSION
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. LOAD PACKAGES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. LOAD DATA
# ------------------------------------------------------------

df <- read_csv(
  "Graph_3_Weighted_Drift_Improvement.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. PREPARE DATA
#
# IMPORTANT:
# - Original improvement values are NOT changed.
# - Original q-values are NOT changed.
# - Packet loss is multiplied by 100 only for display.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

df <- df %>%
  mutate(

    # Convert probability to percentage for x-axis
    loss_percent = loss_probability * 100,

    # Clean signal labels
    signal_label = recode(
      signal,
      "Temp"  = "Temperature",
      "Moist" = "Soil moisture"
    ),

    # Clean feedback labels
    feedback_label = recode(
      feedback_model,
      "ack"    = "ACK",
      "no_ack" = "No ACK"
    ),

    # Asterisk based on SAVED adjusted q-value
    significance = ifelse(
      !is.na(q_value) & q_value < 0.05,
      "*",
      ""
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. CHECK SIGNIFICANT RESULTS
#
# This lets you verify exactly which cells receive *
# ------------------------------------------------------------

significant_cells <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(q_value) & q_value < 0.05) %>%
  select(
    signal,
    feedback_model,
    loss_probability,
    threshold_multiplier,
    aggregate_relative_improvement_percent,
    q_value
  )

print(significant_cells)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. CHECK MISSING IMPROVEMENT VALUES
#
# These cells will appear gray in the heatmap.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

missing_cells <- df %>%
  filter(is.na(aggregate_relative_improvement_percent))

print(missing_cells)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. CREATE SYMMETRIC COLOR LIMIT
#
# Equal positive and negative values receive equal color
# intensity around zero.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

colour_limit <- max(
  abs(df$aggregate_relative_improvement_percent),
  na.rm = TRUE
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. CREATE HEATMAP
# ------------------------------------------------------------

graph3 <- ggplot(
  df,
  aes(
    x = factor(loss_percent),
    y = factor(threshold_multiplier)
  )
) +

  # Heatmap cells
  geom_tile(
    aes(
      fill = aggregate_relative_improvement_percent
    ),
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +

  # Statistical significance marker
  # * means adjusted q-value < 0.05
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = significance
    ),
    colour = "black",
    size = 5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +

  # Four panels:
  # Soil moisture / ACK
  # Soil moisture / No ACK
  # Temperature / ACK
  # Temperature / No ACK
  facet_grid(
    signal_label ~ feedback_label
  ) +

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # DIVERGING COLOR SCALE
  #
  # Blue  = negative relative improvement
  # White = approximately zero
  # Red   = positive relative improvement
  # Gray  = missing/not available
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#2166AC",
    mid = "white",
    high = "#B2182B",

    midpoint = 0,

    limits = c(
      -colour_limit,
      colour_limit
    ),

    oob = squish,

    na.value = "grey60",

    name = "Relative\nimprovement (%)"
  ) +

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # AXIS AND CAPTION
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  labs(
    x = "Packet loss probability (%)",
    y = "Threshold multiplier",

    caption = paste0(
      "* Adjusted q-value < 0.05. ",
      "Gray cells indicate unavailable relative-improvement values."
    )
  ) +

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # PUBLICATION THEME
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  theme_classic(
    base_size = 12
  ) +

  theme(

    # Axis titles
    axis.title.x = element_text(
      size = 12,
      face = "bold",
      margin = margin(t = 8)
    ),

    axis.title.y = element_text(
      size = 12,
      face = "bold",
      margin = margin(r = 8)
    ),

    # Axis numbers
    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 10,
      colour = "black"
    ),

    # Facet headers
    strip.background = element_rect(
      fill = "grey95",
      colour = "black",
      linewidth = 0.6
    ),

    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 11,
      face = "bold",
      colour = "black"
    ),

    # Color legend
    legend.position = "right",

    legend.title = element_text(
      size = 10,
      face = "bold"
    ),

    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 9
    ),

    # Caption explaining *
    plot.caption = element_text(
      size = 9,
      colour = "black",
      hjust = 0,
      margin = margin(t = 10)
    ),

    # Panel border
    panel.border = element_rect(
      colour = "black",
      fill = NA,
      linewidth = 0.6
    ),

    # No unnecessary grid
    panel.grid = element_blank(),

    # Figure margins
    plot.margin = margin(
      10, 10, 10, 10
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. DISPLAY FINAL GRAPH
# ------------------------------------------------------------

print(graph3)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. SAVE HIGH-RESOLUTION PNG
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggsave(
  filename =
    "Graph_3_Weighted_Drift_Improvement.png",

  plot = graph3,

  width = 9,
  height = 7,
  units = "in",

  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. SAVE VECTOR PDF
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggsave(
  filename =
    "Graph_3_Weighted_Drift_Improvement.pdf",

  plot = graph3,

  width = 9,
  height = 7,
  units = "in"
)
```


```{r accuracy-freshness-communication, include=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# GRAPH 4: ACCURACY-FRESHNESS-COMMUNICATION TRADE-OFF
# FINAL PUBLICATION VERSION
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. LOAD PACKAGES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. LOAD DATA
# ------------------------------------------------------------

df <- read_csv(
  "Graph_4_Accuracy_Freshness_Communication.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

View(df)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. PREPARE DATA
# Original numerical values are NOT changed
# ------------------------------------------------------------

df <- df %>%
  mutate(

    signal_label = recode(
      signal,
      "Temp"  = "Temperature",
      "Moist" = "Soil moisture"
    ),

    feedback_label = recode(
      feedback_model,
      "ack"    = "ACK",
      "no_ack" = "No ACK"
    ),

    estimator_label = recode(
      estimator,
      "hold"           = "Hold",
      "weighted_drift" = "Weighted drift"
    ),

    # Fix order for consistent plotting/legend
    feedback_label = factor(
      feedback_label,
      levels = c("ACK", "No ACK")
    ),

    estimator_label = factor(
      estimator_label,
      levels = c("Hold", "Weighted drift")
    )
  ) %>%

  # IMPORTANT:
  # Points are connected in threshold order
  arrange(
    signal,
    feedback_model,
    estimator,
    threshold_multiplier
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. PUBLICATION THEME
# ------------------------------------------------------------

theme_pub <- theme_classic(base_size = 12) +

  theme(

    axis.title = element_text(
      size = 12,
      face = "bold"
    ),

    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 10,
      colour = "black"
    ),

    strip.background = element_rect(
      fill = "grey95",
      colour = "black",
      linewidth = 0.6
    ),

    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 11,
      face = "bold",
      colour = "black"
    ),

    legend.position = "top",

    legend.title = element_text(
      size = 10,
      face = "bold"
    ),

    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 10
    ),

    panel.border = element_rect(
      colour = "black",
      fill = NA,
      linewidth = 0.6
    ),

    panel.grid = element_blank(),

    plot.margin = margin(
      6, 8, 6, 8
    )
  )


# ============================================================
# 5. UPPER PANELS: MSE
# ============================================================

p_mse <- ggplot(
  df,
  aes(
    x = attempted_update_rate_per_minute_mean,
    y = mse_mean,

    # ACK / No ACK by colour
    colour = feedback_label,

    # Hold / Weighted drift by line style
    linetype = estimator_label,

    group = interaction(
      feedback_label,
      estimator_label
    )
  )
) +

  # Connect observations in threshold order
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +

  # Data points
  geom_point(
    size = 2.5
  ) +

  # Temperature and soil moisture panels
  facet_wrap(
    ~ signal_label,
    scales = "free_y",
    nrow = 1
  ) +

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # COLOR-BLIND-SAFE COLORS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "ACK"    = "#0072B2",
      "No ACK" = "#D55E00"
    )
  ) +

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # LINE TYPES
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(
      "Hold"           = "solid",
      "Weighted drift" = "dashed"
    )
  ) +

  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean squared error (MSE)",
    colour = "Feedback",
    linetype = "Estimator"
  ) +

  theme_pub


# ============================================================
# 6. LOWER PANELS: MEAN AoI
#
# IMPORTANT:
# Only HOLD is used here because AoI/channel results are
# repeated across estimators in the CSV.
# ============================================================

df_aoi <- df %>%

  filter(
    estimator == "hold"
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    signal,
    feedback_model,
    threshold_multiplier
  )


p_aoi <- ggplot(
  df_aoi,
  aes(
    x = attempted_update_rate_per_minute_mean,
    y = mean_aoi_minutes_mean,

    colour = feedback_label,

    group = feedback_label
  )
) +

  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +

  geom_point(
    size = 2.5
  ) +

  facet_wrap(
    ~ signal_label,
    scales = "free_y",
    nrow = 1
  ) +

  # Same ACK / No ACK colors as upper panels
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "ACK"    = "#0072B2",
      "No ACK" = "#D55E00"
    )
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Attempted update rate (packets/min)",
    y = "Mean AoI (min)",
    colour = "Feedback"
  ) +

  theme_pub


# ============================================================
# 7. COMBINE UPPER AND LOWER PANELS
# ============================================================

graph4 <- p_mse / p_aoi +

  plot_layout(
    heights = c(1, 1),
    guides = "collect"
  ) &

  theme(
    legend.position = "top"
  )


# ============================================================
# 8. DISPLAY GRAPH
# ============================================================

print(graph4)


# ============================================================
# 9. SAVE HIGH-RESOLUTION PNG
# ============================================================

ggsave(
  filename =
    "Graph_4_Accuracy_Freshness_Communication.png",

  plot = graph4,

  width = 9,
  height = 7,
  units = "in",

  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)


# ============================================================
# 10. SAVE VECTOR PDF
# ============================================================

ggsave(
  filename =
    "Graph_4_Accuracy_Freshness_Communication.pdf",

  plot = graph4,

  width = 9,
  height = 7,
  units = "in"
)
```



```{r deadline-freshness-violations, include=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# GRAPH 5: DEADLINE FRESHNESS VIOLATIONS
# FINAL PUBLICATION VERSION
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. LOAD PACKAGES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. LOAD DATA
# ------------------------------------------------------------

df <- read_csv(
  "Graph_5_Deadline_Freshness_Violations.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

View(df)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. PREPARE DATA
#
# IMPORTANT:
# Original mean and confidence intervals are NOT recalculated.
# Multiplication by 100 is only to display them as percentages.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

df <- df %>%

  # Keep only requested deadline multipliers
  filter(
    freshness_deadline_multiplier %in% c(2, 3, 6)
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    # Packet loss as percentage
    loss_percent =
      loss_probability * 100,

    # Freshness violation rate as percentage
    violation_percent =
      freshness_violation_rate_mean * 100,

    # Confidence intervals as percentages
    violation_ci_low_percent =
      freshness_violation_rate_ci_low * 100,

    violation_ci_high_percent =
      freshness_violation_rate_ci_high * 100,

    # Deadline labels
    deadline = factor(
      freshness_deadline_multiplier,
      levels = c(2, 3, 6),
      labels = c("2×", "3×", "6×")
    ),

    # Signal labels
    signal_label = recode(
      signal,
      "Temp"  = "Temperature",
      "Moist" = "Soil moisture"
    ),

    # Feedback labels
    feedback_label = recode(
      feedback_model,
      "ack"    = "ACK",
      "no_ack" = "No ACK"
    )
  ) %>%

  # Ensure points are connected in packet-loss order
  arrange(
    signal,
    feedback_model,
    freshness_deadline_multiplier,
    loss_probability
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. CREATE GRAPH
# ------------------------------------------------------------

graph5 <- ggplot(
  df,
  aes(
    x = loss_percent,
    y = violation_percent,

    colour = deadline,
    shape = deadline,
    linetype = deadline,

    group = deadline
  )
) +

  # Connecting curves
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +

  # Saved confidence intervals
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = violation_ci_low_percent,
      ymax = violation_ci_high_percent
    ),
    width = 1.0,
    linewidth = 0.45,
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +

  # Mean values
  geom_point(
    size = 2.6,
    stroke = 0.7
  ) +

  # Four requested panels
  facet_grid(
    signal_label ~ feedback_label
  ) +

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # PUBLICATION-FRIENDLY COLORS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "2×" = "#0072B2",
      "3×" = "#D55E00",
      "6×" = "#009E73"
    )
  ) +

  # Different shapes for grayscale accessibility
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(
      "2×" = 16,
      "3×" = 17,
      "6×" = 15
    )
  ) +

  # Different line types as an additional visual cue
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(
      "2×" = "solid",
      "3×" = "dashed",
      "6×" = "dotdash"
    )
  ) +

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # X AXIS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 50, 10),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0.02, 0.04)
    )
  ) +

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # LABELS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  labs(
    x = "Packet loss probability (%)",
    y = "Freshness violation rate (%)",
    colour = "Deadline multiplier",
    shape = "Deadline multiplier",
    linetype = "Deadline multiplier"
  ) +

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # PUBLICATION THEME
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  theme_classic(
    base_size = 12
  ) +

  theme(

    # Axis titles
    axis.title = element_text(
      size = 12,
      face = "bold"
    ),

    # Axis values
    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 10,
      colour = "black"
    ),

    # Facet headers
    strip.background = element_rect(
      fill = "grey95",
      colour = "black",
      linewidth = 0.6
    ),

    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 11,
      face = "bold",
      colour = "black"
    ),

    # Legend
    legend.position = "top",

    legend.title = element_text(
      size = 10,
      face = "bold"
    ),

    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 10
    ),

    # Panel border
    panel.border = element_rect(
      colour = "black",
      fill = NA,
      linewidth = 0.6
    ),

    # Remove unnecessary grid
    panel.grid = element_blank(),

    # Margins
    plot.margin = margin(
      8, 8, 8, 8
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. DISPLAY GRAPH
# ------------------------------------------------------------

print(graph5)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. SAVE HIGH-RESOLUTION PNG
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggsave(
  filename =
    "Graph_5_Deadline_Freshness_Violations.png",

  plot = graph5,

  width = 8.5,
  height = 6.5,
  units = "in",

  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. SAVE VECTOR PDF
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggsave(
  filename =
    "Graph_5_Deadline_Freshness_Violations.pdf",

  plot = graph5,

  width = 8.5,
  height = 6.5,
  units = "in"
)
```
